# Software

All labs use **STATA** on your own laptop. The course do-files use official Stata commands (`regress`, `teffects`, `sem`, `xtreg`, `ivregress`, `margins`, `permute`). If your Stata is older than the version declared at the top of a do-file (`version ...`), change that line to your own version.

## User-written packages

Only one user-written command is used in the labs (`fre`, Session 2, which `tab1` can replace); the others are optional conveniences mentioned in the do-files:

``` stata
* Session 2 — frequency tables with labels (or use tab1)
ssc install fre, replace

* Sessions 3 and 4 — coefficient plots
ssc install coefplot, replace

* Session 4 — fast regressions with many fixed effects
ssc install ftools, replace
ssc install reghdfe, replace
```

If `ssc install` fails on the university network, try again from a different connection or download the package files from [SSC](https://ideas.repec.org/s/boc/bocode.html) and install them with `net install`.

## Working with replicable code

Assignments and the final paper must be accompanied by a do-file that reproduces all results. A minimal structure:

``` stata
* ------------------------------------------------------------
* Project:  <title>
* Author:   <name>
* Date:     <date>
* Purpose:  reproduces all tables and figures in the paper
* ------------------------------------------------------------
version 18
clear all
set more off
set seed 20262027

* Paths: change only this line
global root "C:/Users/<you>/qmm2627_assignment1"

use "$root/data/mydata.dta", clear

* 1. Data preparation
* 2. Descriptives
* 3. Main models
* 4. Robustness and diagnostics
```

Set `version` to the Stata version you use, always set a seed when results depend on randomization (bootstrap, randomization inference, matching with ties), and never hard-code paths inside the analysis.

# Open-access texts

-   Huntington-Klein, N. (2022). *The Effect: An Introduction to Research Design and Causality*. <https://theeffectbook.net>
-   Cunningham, S. (2021). *Causal Inference: The Mixtape*. <https://mixtape.scunning.com>

# Data used in the labs

The data are distributed with the materials of each session. Most are teaching versions of published replication datasets.

| Session | Data | Source |
|:-------:|------|--------|
| 1 | Simulated data from a known causal diagram | Created in the do-file |
| 2 | Role of government items, NLSY97 | Acock (2013), ch. 1 and sec. 5.3 |
| 3 | Anchoring vignettes; list experiment; social pressure and turnout | King et al. (2004); Blair, Imai & Lyall (2014); Gerber, Green & Larimer (2008), as in Imai & Bougher (2021) |
| 3 | Immigration conjoint | Hainmueller, Hopkins & Yamamoto (2014) |
| 4 | Minimum wage in New Jersey and Pennsylvania | Card & Krueger (1994), as in Imai & Bougher (2021) |
| 5 | College proximity and earnings | Card (1995), as in Cunningham (2021) |
| 5, 6 | Wealth at death of British MP candidates | Eggers & Hainmueller (2009), as in Imai & Bougher (2021) |
| 6 | Life expectancy and income, 1998 | Shipped with Stata: `sysuse lifeexp` |
